newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish government deficit target stands - Asbrink.
newsitem.headline: Swedish government deficit target stands - Asbrink.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Friday the government still planned to eliminate the country's budget deficit by 1998 despite a pledge to increase welfare spending by 10 billion crowns.

Asbrink told Swedish radio that financial markets -- which marked the crown down sharply in reaction to Prime Minister Goran Persson's spending commitment -- had been given a shock by the announcement.
"The target is to get rid of the budget deficit by 1998 and have a surplus in 1999 and onwards," he said.
Asbrink said the government had calculated the 10 billion crowns it estimated it could make available for extra spending in 1998, when a general election will be held.
"Of course we cannot be precise, but everything points towards a positive outcome. We will find the 10 billion crowns needed and still get rid of the deficit next year," he added.

Persson's plan to spend more money on social services has worried financial markets, which fear that a tough, two-year programme of fiscal control may be reversed to allow Persson to win the general election.
